mainTopic: ביקור חולים: its source, its measure and its effect, with דרשות about קרח and משה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof from the משנה's wording: the visitor may stand but not sit, which shows that the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person. ריש לקיש then finds a רמז for ביקור חולים in משה's words about קרח, and רבא explains that a normal death includes lying sick in bed while people visit. רבא also explains 'בריאה יברא': if גיהנם exists, good, and if not, ה׳ should create it. A ברייתא says גיהנם was created before the world, so the גמרא re-reads the words as being about the mouth of גיהנם. In the end, משה was asking ה׳ to bring the existing mouth close. Another דרשה tells how the sun and moon stood up for משה, and how ה׳ rebuked them for caring more about a human's honor than His own. The גמרא then returns to ביקור חולים: it has no measure, meaning even a great person visits a lesser one (אביי) or one may visit even a hundred times a day (רבא). A visitor takes away one-sixtieth of the remaining pain, which is explained through רבי's rule of tenths for daughters. The amud ends as רב חלבו falls ill and רב כהנא begins an announcement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the wording 'stands but does not sit'
steps.stepSummary: The one who holds that the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person proves it from the משנה's wording: the visitor may stand but not sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He found the משנה hard to explain: why does it say specifically that the visitor stands but does not sit? This shows that the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this opinion holds that the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person. The reason is the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the visitor may enter and stand, but may not sit. If only the sick person's property were forbidden to the visitor, there would seem to be no reason to single out sitting. So the wording points to the other direction: the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה was difficult for him
Why specifically? Why mention this case?
Learn from it, conclude from it

phrases.english: The mishna was difficult for him;
phrases.notes: "Him" is the one from just before this, who said the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person.

phrases.english: why does it specifically teach
"he stands but does not sit"?
Conclude from it that the property of the visitor
is forbidden to the sick person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from before this part of the daf about whose property is forbidden to whom.
steps.raayaObject: That the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording: עומד אבל לא יושב
steps.whatToRemember: The extra detail 'stands but does not sit' is read as showing that the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person.

steps.title: A hint in the תורה for visiting the sick
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says there is a רמז for ביקור חולים in משה's words about קרח and his group.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Where is there a hint in the תורה for visiting the sick? From the פסוק: 'If these men die like all people die, and are visited the way all people are visited...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching connected to visiting the sick. ריש לקיש points to a פסוק as a hint for this מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the word רמז, meaning a hint rather than a direct command. The פסוק is משה speaking about קרח's group. He does not yet explain which part of the פסוק is the hint, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint or allusion in the פסוק

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A hint for visiting the sick
from the Torah, from where?
As it says: "If like the death of all men
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:29

phrases.english: these men die
and the visiting of all men, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: רֶמֶז לְבִיקּוּר חוֹלִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to visiting the sick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a hint in the תורה for ביקור חולים from the פסוק about קרח.

steps.title: Where in the verse is the hint?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this פסוק shows visiting the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this show it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what in the פסוק hints to ביקור חולים. It is setting up רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on ריש לקיש. It is a request to explain how the פסוק is being read.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it show? How is this implied?

phrases.english: What does it show?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of ריש לקיש's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק hints to ביקור חולים

steps.title: רבא explains: a normal death includes being visited
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains משה's words: if קרח's group die normally, sick in bed with people visiting them, people will say ה׳ did not send משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'If these men die like all people die': they are sick, lying in their beds, and people visit them. Then what will people say? 'ה׳ did not send me for this.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He describes a normal death as becoming sick, lying in bed, and having people visit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'the visiting of all men' as people coming to visit the sick. Since the פסוק treats being visited as part of the normal human path, it hints that visiting the sick is the normal and proper thing. משה's point was that if קרח's group died this ordinary way, people would say he was not sent by ה׳.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"If like the death of all men
these men die,"
that they are sick and lying in their beds,
and people visit them,
what will people say?
"The Lord did not send me for this."
phrases.notes: These are משה's words. People would say ה׳ did not send him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם כְּמוֹת כׇּל הָאָדָם יְמוּתוּן אֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A normal death means being sick in bed and visited by people, so the פסוק treats visiting the sick as the normal way of the world.
steps.whatToRemember: The hint for ביקור חולים is 'ופקודת כל האדם': normally, sick people are visited.

steps.title: If גיהנם exists, good; if not, let ה׳ create it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the double wording 'בריאה יברא' in the next פסוק: if גיהנם already exists, good; if not, ה׳ should create it now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: 'If ה׳ will create a creation.' If גיהנם is already created, good. If not, 'let ה׳ create' it.
steps.whatsHappening: Still talking about קרח, רבא explains the next פסוק. He reads the doubled word 'create, create' as two possibilities about גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He divides the words: 'אם בריאה' means 'if גיהנם is already a creation,' that is fine. 'יברא ה׳' means 'if not, ה׳ should create it now,' so that קרח's group can be swallowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Explained a פסוק as a drasha

phrases.english: Rava taught:
"If the Lord will create a creation":
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:30

phrases.english: "If" Gehinnom is already "a creation,"
good, let it be;
if not, "let the Lord create" it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: אִם בְּרִיאָה יִבְרָא ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another teaching about the same story of קרח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה said: if גיהנם exists, good; if not, ה׳ should create it now.

steps.title: But גיהנם was created before the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא listing seven things created before the world, including גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But a ברייתא teaches: Seven things were created before the world was created: תורה, תשובה, גן עדן, גיהנם, כסא הכבוד, בית המקדש, and the name of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's drasha. How could משה be unsure whether גיהנם existed, if it was created before the world?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reading treats it as an open question whether גיהנם had already been created. The ברייתא clearly says גיהנם existed before the world. Step 10 answers this challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so? But it is taught:
Seven things were created
before the world was created,
and these are they: Torah, and repentance,
the Garden of Eden, and Gehinnom,
the Throne of Glory, and the Temple,
and the name of the Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's drasha in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that it was uncertain whether גיהנם existed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says גיהנם was created before the world, so there should be no question whether it already existed in משה's time.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא's question is only about גיהנם. The other six items show the full list of the ברייתא, but they are not part of the question.

steps.title: Sources for תורה, תשובה, and גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק for each item to prove that תורה, תשובה and גן עדן were created before the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה was made before the world, as it says: 'ה׳ made me as the beginning of His way.' תשובה was made before the world, as it says: 'Before the mountains were born…', and right after that: 'You return man to contrition.' גן עדן was made before the world, as it says: 'ה׳ planted a garden in Eden מִקֶּדֶם (from before).'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still talking. It goes through its list of things created before the world and gives a פסוק as proof for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each proof works a little differently. The תורה 'speaks' and says it came first. Returning to ה׳ (תשובה) is mentioned right next to 'before the mountains were born'. The word מִקֶּדֶם is read as 'from before' and not only as 'eastward'.

keyTerms.meaning: He made me / acquired me. Here the Torah is the one speaking.
The beginning of His way, meaning the first thing ה׳ made
Eastward, or 'from before'. The ברייתא reads it as 'from before'.

phrases.english: Torah, as it is written: 'The Lord'
'made me as the beginning of His way, etc.'
phrases.notes: משלי 8:22. The 'me' here is the Torah talking about itself.

phrases.english: Repentance, as it is written:
'Before the mountains were brought forth, or You had formed, etc.'
'You return man to contrition, etc.'
phrases.notes: This is the very next פסוק (תהלים 90:3). So 'returning' is placed right next to 'before the mountains'.

phrases.english: The Garden of Eden, as it is written:
'And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden'
'eastward, etc.'
phrases.notes: מִקֶּדֶם can also mean 'from before'. The proof reads it that way: before the world was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 6 by giving the פסוק behind each item on its list.
steps.raayaObject: That תורה, תשובה and גן עדן were created before the world

steps.title: Source that גיהנם was created before the world
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from a פסוק that גיהנם was already prepared before the world was made. This is the point that clashes with רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גיהנם was made before the world, as it says: 'For its hearth (תָּפְתֶּה) is prepared from yesterday.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its proof that גיהנם existed before the world. This is the item that makes trouble for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said 'if גיהנם already exists, good; if not, let ה׳ create it now'. That only makes sense if we are not sure whether גיהנם exists. This פסוק says it was ready 'from yesterday', meaning before the world. So there seems to be no doubt for רבא to talk about.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment for the wicked
From yesterday, meaning from long ago, before the world
Its hearth. Another name for גיהנם.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says גיהנם was created before the world. That seems to cancel out רבא's 'if not, let ה׳ create it now'. The גמרא now needs to answer this.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is disagreeing with the whole idea of the קרח story. It only challenges one detail in רבא's reading: the doubt about whether גיהנם already existed.

phrases.english: Gehenna, as it is written:
'For its hearth is prepared from yesterday.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:33. 'From yesterday' is read as 'from before the world existed', and the hearth is גיהנם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list with the one item that directly clashes with רבא in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of בריאה יברא in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If גיהנם was prepared before the world, there is no room to say 'if it doesn't exist, let ה׳ create it now'.
steps.raayaObject: That גיהנם was created before the world

steps.title: The last three items: כסא כבוד, בית המקדש, and the name of משיח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove that the כסא כבוד, the בית המקדש and the name of משיח were created before the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כסא כבוד, as it is written: 'Your throne is established from of old.' The בית המקדש, as it is written: 'A Throne of Glory, on high from the beginning.' The name of משיח, as it is written: 'May his name be forever, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of seven things, giving a פסוק for each of the last three. Once the list is done, the clash with רבא stands fully in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק uses a word that means 'from long ago' or 'from the beginning' (מֵאָז, מֵרִאשׁוֹן, or a name lasting before the sun). These items add nothing new to the clash with רבא, which was about גיהנם in step 8. They complete the list so the ברייתא is quoted in full before the גמרא answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The Throne of Glory, ה׳'s heavenly throne
From of old, from long ago
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: The Throne of Glory, as it is written:
"Your throne is established from of old."
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:2

phrases.english: The Temple, as it is written:
"A Throne of Glory, on high from the beginning."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 17:12. The פסוק goes on to say 'the place of our מקדש', which is why it proves the מקדש.

phrases.english: The name of משיח, as it is written:
"May his name be forever, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:17. The rest of the פסוק says his name existed before the sun, which was made at creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of proofs from steps 7 and 8, finishing the last three items.
steps.raayaObject: That the כסא כבוד, the בית המקדש and the name of משיח existed before the world

steps.title: משה was asking about the mouth of גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads רבא: משה said that if a mouth (opening) had already been created for גיהנם, good; if not, ה׳ should create one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he is saying: if a mouth was created for it, good; and if not, 'let ה׳ create' it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא's challenge by changing what משה was unsure about. He was not asking whether גיהנם exists, only whether it already has an opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says גיהנם itself existed before the world, so רבא cannot mean that גיהנם might not exist yet. The new reading moves the doubt to the 'mouth' of גיהנם. That keeps the double wording 'בריאה יברא' as two options while agreeing with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier reading is being replaced

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is rejecting רבא completely. It keeps his idea of two options ('if yes, good; if not, create'). It only changes what the doubt is about: the opening, not גיהנם itself.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is משה, as רבא explains him.

phrases.english: If a mouth was already created for it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means גיהנם, and the 'mouth' is the opening that swallows people.

phrases.english: good;
and if not, "let ה׳ create" it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא, which steps 6 to 9 quoted in full.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-interpretation: the doubt is moved from גיהנם itself to its opening
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה was unsure whether גיהנם existed at all
steps.terutzMaskana: גיהנם existed; משה was unsure whether its mouth had been created

steps.title: Nothing is new under the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: קהלת says nothing is new under the sun, so how could ה׳ create a new mouth for גיהנם now?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'There is nothing new under the sun'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, using a פסוק that says nothing new is created after creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading still has משה asking ה׳ to create something new, an opening, in his own time. The פסוק in קהלת suggests that nothing truly new comes into being after the six days. So the second option, 'if not, let ה׳ create', seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? It brings a פסוק as a challenge
There is nothing new under the sun

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"There is nothing new under the sun"!
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:9

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: אֵין כׇּל חָדָשׁ תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that משה asked ה׳ to create a mouth for גיהנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Creating a new opening would be something new under the sun, and the פסוק says that cannot happen

steps.title: Bring the existing mouth closer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה meant: if the mouth of גיהנם is not near here, let ה׳ bring it close to here.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: if the mouth is not close to here, let it come close to here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading משה as asking ה׳ to move the existing opening, not to make a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving something that already exists is not creating something new, so the פסוק in קהלת is not broken. The double wording now means 'if the opening is already here, good; if not, bring it here.' That fits רבא, the ברייתא, and קהלת together.
steps.whatToRemember: The final reading of 'בריאה יברא': גיהנם and its mouth already existed. משה asked that, if the mouth was not right where קרח's group stood, ה׳ would bring it there.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If the mouth is not close to here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the place where קרח's group was standing.

phrases.english: let it come close to here.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִי הָכָא לָא מְקָרַב פּוּמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from קהלת in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-interpretation: 'create' is read as moving something that already exists, not making something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה asked ה׳ to create a new opening for גיהנם
steps.terutzMaskana: משה asked ה׳ to bring the existing opening close to קרח's group
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nothing new was created; the already-existing mouth of גיהנם was brought to the right place.

steps.title: Why would the sun and moon be in זבול?
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יצחק) asks about a פסוק that puts the sun and moon in זבול, when they really belong in רקיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught (some say it was רבי יצחק): What does the פסוק mean, 'The sun and moon stood in זבול'? What are the sun and moon doing in זבול? They are set in רקיע!
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching on the משה and קרח story starts with a question about a פסוק. The question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sun and moon are fixed in the heaven called רקיע. So a פסוק saying they 'stood in זבול', a higher heaven, seems strange. The odd wording is the opening for a דרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught a lesson drawn from a פסוק
And some say (a second version of who said it)
The heaven where the sun and moon are set

phrases.english: Rava taught,
and some say Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
“The sun and moon stood still in זבול”?
phrases.notes: חבקוק 3:11

phrases.english: What are the sun and moon doing in זבול?
But they are set in רקיע!
phrases.notes: רקיע and זבול are two different heavens. The sun and moon belong in רקיע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another דרשה about משה and קרח after the discussion of the mouth of גיהנם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק place the sun and moon in זבול instead of רקיע?

steps.title: The sun and moon went up to stand for משה
steps.stepSummary: The sun and moon went up to זבול and told ה׳ they would not shine unless He did justice for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that the sun and moon went up from רקיע to זבול and said before Him: Master of the world, if You do justice for the son of עמרם, we will shine. If not, we will not shine.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question. The sun and moon left their place on purpose to make a demand on משה's behalf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strange word 'זבולה' now makes sense: they went up there to stand before ה׳. Their demand was that ה׳ show the world that משה was right against קרח.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the פסוק comes to teach)
The son of עמרם, meaning משה
Do justice, stand up for someone

phrases.english: It teaches that the sun and moon went up
from רקיע to זבול, and said before Him:
Master of the world,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה דִּין לְבֶן עַמְרָם —
phrases.english: if You do justice for the son of Amram,
phrases.notes: That's משה, in his fight with קרח.

phrases.english: we will shine,
and if not, we will not shine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word זבולה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They went up to זבול to demand justice for משה, threatening not to shine.

steps.title: ה׳ rebukes the sun and moon
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ shot arrows and spears at them. He scolded them for protesting for a human's honor but never for His own honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment He shot arrows and spears at them and said: Every day people bow down to you, and you keep shining. For My honor you never protested, but for the honor of flesh and blood you protest?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. ה׳ answers the sun and moon's demand with a sharp rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People worship the sun and moon every day, which is an insult to ה׳, yet they never stopped shining over it. So threatening to stop shining for משה's sake showed they had their priorities backward.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.english: At that moment He shot at them
arrows and spears, and said to them:
Every single day people bow down to you
and you keep shining.
For My honor you did not protest,
but for the honor of flesh and blood you protest?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה יָרָה בָּהֶן חִיצִּים וַחֲנִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with ה׳'s response to the sun and moon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ rebuked the sun and moon for protesting over a human's honor but not over His own.

steps.title: Every day they are pushed to shine
steps.stepSummary: From then on, arrows and spears are shot at them every day before they shine, as the rest of the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And every day arrows and spears are shot at them, and only then do they shine, as it says: 'By the light of Your arrows they go, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the story and backs it up with the second half of the same פסוק in חבקוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words about 'Your arrows' and 'Your spear' in the פסוק show that the arrows are real and happen daily. Now the whole פסוק is explained: the first half is about going up to זבול, and the second half is about the arrows.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (a פסוק is brought as proof)
By the light of Your arrows

phrases.english: And every single day they shoot at them
arrows and spears, and then they shine,
as it says: “By the light of Your arrows they go, etc.”
phrases.notes: חבקוק 3:11, the same פסוק we started with.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם יוֹרִין בָּהֶן חִיצִּין וַחֲנִיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves from the rest of the פסוק that the arrows continue every day.
steps.raayaObject: That arrows and spears are shot at the sun and moon every day before they shine.
steps.whatToRemember: The sun and moon stood up for משה. ה׳ rebuked them for caring more about a human's honor than His own, and ever since they shine only after being pushed with arrows.

steps.title: Visiting the sick has no measure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the מצוה of ביקור חולים has no fixed measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: Visiting the sick has no measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main topic, ביקור חולים, and quotes a ברייתא. This sets up a discussion about what the words 'no measure' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say what kind of 'measure' it means. Is it the reward, who must visit, or how often? The next steps try to pin this down.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: Visiting the sick
has no measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: בִּיקּוּר חוֹלִים אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to the topic of ביקור חולים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of ביקור חולים has no fixed measure.

steps.title: What does 'no measure' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'no measure'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'has no measure' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means. This opens the door to the different answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the wording. 'Measure' could point to many things, so the גמרא needs to know which one is meant.

phrases.english: What does “has no measure” mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא's words mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of 'measure' does the ברייתא mean?

steps.title: רב יוסף: no limit to its reward
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף first thought it means the reward for ביקור חולים has no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף thought to say: There is no measure to its reward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a first answer. The words 'סבר למימר' ('thought to say') hint that this answer will not hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף reads 'measure' as the size of the reward. On his reading, ביקור חולים would be special because its reward is endless.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a first idea that is later dropped)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
there is no measure to the giving of its reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No measure means the reward is unlimited.

steps.title: אביי: no מצוה has a known reward
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף using a משנה in אבות: we never know the reward of any מצוה, so this would not make ביקור חולים special.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do all other מצוות have a measure for their reward? But we learned in a משנה: Be as careful with a light מצוה as with a serious one, because you do not know the reward for מצוות!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no מצוה has a known reward, then saying ביקור חולים has 'no measure to its reward' tells us nothing new. The ברייתא must mean something that is special to this מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And do all other מצוות have a measure
for the giving of their reward?
But we learned in a משנה:
Be as careful with a light מצוה as with a serious one,
phrases.notes: אבות 2:1

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ מַתַּן שְׂכָרָן שֶׁל מִצְוֹת!
phrases.english: because you do not know the reward of מצוות!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִצְוֹת מִי יֵשׁ שִׁיעוּר לְמַתַּן שְׂכָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading that 'no measure' refers to the reward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No מצוה has a known reward, so this reading would make the ברייתא's statement about ביקור חולים pointless.

steps.title: אביי: even a great person visits a lesser one
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains: 'no measure' means there is no limit on who should visit. Even an important person visits someone lower than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Even a great person should visit a lesser person.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יוסף, אביי offers his own meaning for 'no measure'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the 'measure' is the difference in status between the visitor and the sick person. No status gap is big enough to excuse someone from visiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (bringing a new answer in place of the one rejected)
A great person going to a lesser person

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Even a great person goes to a lesser one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No measure' was thought to mean the reward has no limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No measure' means no gap in status excuses someone from visiting.

steps.title: רבא: even a hundred times a day
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains 'no measure' as no limit on how many times one visits, even a hundred times a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even a hundred times a day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different meaning for 'no measure' than אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the 'measure' is how often you visit. You do not finish the מצוה with one visit. Each extra visit is another act of the מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say whether אביי and רבא disagree in practice. Each one is explaining a different kind of 'measure' in the same ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: 'ביקור חולים has no measure' does not mean an endless reward, since that is true of every מצוה. אביי says it means no status gap excuses you. רבא says it means there is no limit on how many visits.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even a hundred times a day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second explanation, alongside אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reading of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No measure' means there is no limit on how often one visits.

steps.title: A visitor takes one-sixtieth of the pain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא teaches that whoever visits a sick person takes away one-sixtieth of his suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: Anyone who visits a sick person takes away one-sixtieth of his pain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about how much good ביקור חולים does for the sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a real effect to the visit. It is not only a מצוה for the visitor; it actually lightens the sick person's pain by one part out of sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: One who visits a sick person

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
Anyone who visits a sick person
takes away one-sixtieth of his pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: כׇּל הַמְבַקֵּר חוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching on ביקור חולים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each visitor removes one-sixtieth of the sick person's suffering.

steps.title: Then let sixty people visit and cure him
steps.stepSummary: The listeners challenge him: if so, sixty visitors should remove all the pain and heal him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, let sixty people come in and get him back on his feet!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא's teaching is challenged with simple math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each visitor removes one-sixtieth, then sixty visitors should remove sixty-sixtieths, which is all of the pain. That does not happen, so the teaching seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And stand him up, heal him

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
let sixty people come in and stand him up!
phrases.notes: They mean sixty visitors would take away all his pain and he'd be healthy again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the one-sixtieth teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that each visitor removes one-sixtieth of the pain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sixty visitors would add up to removing all the pain, but that does not happen.

steps.title: Like רבי's tenths, and only someone like him
steps.stepSummary: Each visitor takes a sixtieth of the pain that is left, like the tenths of רבי's school. Also, it works only for a visitor who is his בן גיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It works like the tenths of רבי's school, and only with someone born under his same sign.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא answers the challenge with two points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, each visitor takes one-sixtieth of whatever pain is still left, not of the original amount, so some pain always remains. Second, the effect only happens with a visitor who is his בן גיל, so not every visitor counts.

keyTerms.meaning: One born under the same sign as him

steps.whatToRemember: A visitor lightens the sick person's pain by one-sixtieth of what remains, and only a בן גיל has this effect. So many visitors help a lot, but the pain never fully runs out this way.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Like the tenths of the school of Rabbi,
phrases.notes: In רבי's case each daughter takes a tenth of what's left. Here each visitor takes a sixtieth of the pain still remaining.

phrases.english: and only by one born under his same sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sixty-visitors challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the calculation works and limits who has the effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each visitor takes one-sixtieth of the original pain, so sixty visitors would remove it all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each visitor takes one-sixtieth of the remaining pain, and only a בן גיל has this effect.

steps.title: רבי's rule: a daughter gets a tenth of the estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to explain 'the tenths of רבי's school.' רבי rules that a daughter supported from her brothers' inheritance receives a tenth of the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: A daughter who is supported from her brothers' property takes a tenth of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind 'the tenths of רבי's school,' which it mentioned in the previous step. רבי says a daughter living off her brothers' inheritance gets one tenth of the estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the father dies, the sons inherit, but the daughters are supported from the estate. רבי sets the daughter's share for her marriage at one tenth. This ruling is the starting point for the challenge and answer that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Who is supported (fed and provided for)
The brothers' property, the estate the sons inherited

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא. The גמרא is showing what 'the tenths of רבי's school' meant in the last step.

phrases.english: A daughter who is supported from the brothers' property
takes a tenth of the property.
phrases.notes: This tenth is her dowry for when she marries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the comparison made in step 25 ('like the tenths of רבי's school').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter supported from her brothers' estate takes one tenth of the property for her dowry.

steps.title: The Sages object: ten daughters would leave the son nothing
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי: if each daughter takes a tenth, then a man with ten daughters and one son would leave the son with nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי: According to your words, if someone has ten daughters and a son, the son gets nothing where there are daughters!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי's rule. If every daughter gets a tenth, ten daughters would take the whole estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is simple math: ten tenths equal everything. But the son is the real heir, so a rule that leaves him nothing cannot be right. This is the same kind of question as in step 24, where sixty visitors would seem to remove all the pain.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words (following your opinion)

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi:
According to your words, one who has
ten daughters and a son,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לַבֵּן בִּמְקוֹם בָּנוֹת כְּלוּם!
phrases.english: the son has nothing at all where there are daughters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's rule from step 26 by pushing it to an extreme case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's rule that each daughter takes a tenth of the estate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ten daughters times one tenth each equals the whole estate, leaving the son, the actual heir, with nothing. That result is absurd.

steps.title: Each daughter takes a tenth of what is left
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that the first daughter takes a tenth of the whole estate, and each later daughter takes a tenth of what remains. Then the daughters pool their shares and divide them equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The first daughter takes a tenth of the property. The second takes a tenth of what the first left. The third takes a tenth of what the second left. Then they go back and split it equally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי explains that each tenth comes from a shrinking remainder, not from the original estate. In the end the daughters share what they took equally, so no daughter loses out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every daughter takes a tenth of a smaller amount, the ten shares never add up to the whole estate, and the son always keeps a real part. Pooling and splitting equally keeps the first daughter from getting more than the last. This is exactly the model for step 25: each visitor takes a sixtieth of the pain that is left, so the pain is never fully removed.

keyTerms.meaning: They go back and divide equally

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think each daughter gets a tenth of the original estate. Each tenth is taken from what remains after the earlier daughters, so the shares keep getting smaller and never use up the whole estate.
steps.whatToRemember: 'A fraction of what remains' never reaches zero. That is how רבי's tenths work, and it is why sixty visitors each removing a sixtieth do not completely heal the sick person.

phrases.english: He said to them:
The first takes a tenth of the property,
the second, a tenth of what she left,
the third, a tenth of what she left,
and then they go back and divide equally.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: רִאשׁוֹנָה נוֹטֶלֶת עִישּׂוּר נְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27 and supplies the model that step 25 relied on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the rule is applied: each fraction is taken from the remainder, not from the original whole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each daughter takes a tenth of the original estate, so ten daughters take it all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each daughter takes a tenth of what is left, so the son always keeps a share, and in the end the daughters divide their total equally.

steps.title: רב חלבו falls ill and רב כהנא makes an announcement
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רב חלבו became sick, and רב כהנא went out to announce something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלבו became ill. רב כהנא went out and announced:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story connected to visiting the sick. This line only sets the scene; what רב כהנא announced comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of visiting the sick now moves from teachings to a real-life story. The reader should expect the announcement to deal with going to visit רב חלבו.

phrases.english: Rav Chelbo became ill.
Rav Kahana went out and announced:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֶלְבּוֹ חֲלַשׁ, נְפַק אַכְרֵיז רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the math of רבי's tenths and begins a story about visiting a sick person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup line only: רב חלבו is sick, and רב כהנא is about to announce something.
